sentences.en: Welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through some of the big life changes and transitions of our 20s and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到《The Psychology of Your 20s》，在这里我们探讨二十岁时面临的一些重大生活变化与转折，以及它们对我们心理的意义。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到节目中。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world.
sentences.zh: 新听众、老听众，无论你身处世界的哪个角落。

sentences.en: It is so great to have you here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能来到这里。

sentences.en: So great to have you here for another episode.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能来收听又一期节目。

sentences.en: One that I'm very, very excited about.
sentences.zh: 这是一个让我感到非常非常兴奋的主题。

sentences.en: This week, we're talking about gossip.
sentences.zh: 本周我们来聊聊八卦。

sentences.en: Something a little bit different, a little bit unusual, but really fascinating nonetheless.
sentences.zh: 这是一个有点与众不同、有点不寻常，但依然非常迷人的话题。

sentences.en: And honestly, when we're talking about our 20s, it's something that is bound to be part of our lives.
sentences.zh: 老实说，当我们谈论二十岁时，八卦注定会成为我们生活的一部分。

sentences.en: Since researching this topic, since thinking about it, I have come to realize and begun to notice how much of my own daily conversations
sentences.zh: 自从研究了这个话题、开始思考它之后，我逐渐意识到并开始注意到，我自己的日常对话中有多少比例

sentences.en: are made up of talking about other people or details of their lives.
sentences.zh: 是由谈论他人或他们生活中的细节组成的。

sentences.en: And I'm sure that it's the same for a lot of us.
sentences.zh: 我相信对于我们很多人来说也是如此。

sentences.en: We may say that we don't gossip.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会说自己不八卦。

sentences.en: We may, you know, try and say that we're above it, that we don't talk about people behind their backs or talk about the things that are going on in their lives.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们可能会试图表现得清高，说我们不会在背后议论别人，也不会谈论他们生活中的事情。

sentences.en: But let's be real.
sentences.zh: 但说实话吧。

sentences.en: Everyone does it.
sentences.zh: 每个人都会这么做。

sentences.en: Gossip is everywhere, even in places that we don't recognize it.
sentences.zh: 八卦无处不在，甚至在我们没有意识到的地方也是如此。

sentences.en: And it's because it is part of our human nature, part of what makes us social beings in very vast social networks across different groups and communities.
sentences.zh: 这是因为它是我们人性的一部分，是我们作为社会人在不同群体和社群庞大社交网络中成为社会性动物的一部分。

sentences.en: But I think what I've come to realize is that there are different levels and different types of gossip.
sentences.zh: 但我想我开始意识到的是，八卦有不同的层级和类型。

sentences.en: And some are obviously more insidious than others.
sentences.zh: 显然，有些比其他的更具潜移默化的恶意。

sentences.en: You know, there's a difference between sharing a story about a friend and their trip to Europe or, you know, their work troubles or what they're up to
sentences.zh: 你知道的，分享一个关于朋友及其欧洲之行、或者是他们的工作烦恼、近况的故事

sentences.en: and saying something spiteful that you know is not true.
sentences.zh: 与说出你明知不是事实的恶毒言论是有区别的。

sentences.en: And I think understanding that distinction is really crucial, along with some of the reasons and the factors that drive us to engage in gossip, whether it's negative or positive.
sentences.zh: 我认为理解这种区别至关重要，同时也要理解驱使我们参与八卦（无论是负面还是正面）的原因和因素。

sentences.en: So I really want to dissect the psychology behind why we gossip, why it's actually a fairly typical and normal thing for us to do,
sentences.zh: 所以我真的很想剖析我们为什么会八卦背后的心理，为什么这其实是一件相当典型和正常的事情，

sentences.en: and the kind of different types of gossip that we will see in our lives and we find ourselves engaging in.
sentences.zh: 以及我们在生活中会看到并发现自己参与的各种不同类型的八卦。

sentences.en: I also want to touch on the role of gossip in our 20s and also how this type of social communication, we might call it,
sentences.zh: 我还想谈谈八卦在我们二十岁时的作用，以及这种社会交流方式——我们可以这样称呼它——

sentences.en: has changed as we've begun sharing so much of our lives on social media and exposing ourselves to potential criticism and gossip online.
sentences.zh: 在我们开始在社交媒体上分享这么多生活、将自己暴露在潜在的批评和网络八卦之下面临的变化。

sentences.en: And I want to talk about how we can stop engaging in this if we would like to, which I hope that we would want to, how we can stop engaging in the more toxic kinds of gossip
sentences.zh: 我想讨论如果我们愿意的话（我希望我们愿意），我们该如何停止参与这种行为，如何停止参与那种更具毒性的八卦，

sentences.en: and how this kind of gossiping, creating rumours, maybe breaking the trust of friends, it's rooted in a lot of insecurity, a lot of negative self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 以及这种八卦、制造谣言、甚至打破朋友信任的行为，是如何根源于大量的不安全感和负面的自尊心。

sentences.en: Gossip, as I've come to realise whilst I've been reading into this, is so nuanced and so fascinating.
sentences.zh: 正如我在阅读相关资料时所意识到的那样，八卦是非常微妙且引人入胜的。

sentences.en: And like I said, really crucial to discuss in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 正如我所说，在我们二十岁时讨论这个话题真的至关重要。

sentences.en: I'm sure we've all had a few moments talking with our friends about something we knew we weren't supposed to know about.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定我们都曾和朋友聊起过一些我们知道自己不该知道的事情。

sentences.en: Maybe you've stretched the truth a little bit to sensationalise a story.
sentences.zh: 也许你为了让故事更耸人听闻而稍微夸大了事实。

sentences.en: Maybe you've had someone say something about you that you know isn't true.
sentences.zh: 也许有人说过关于你的某些事情，而你知道那根本不是真的。

sentences.en: And you know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: Maybe it's uncomfortable to admit to ourselves because gossip definitely gets a bad rap.
sentences.zh: 向自己承认这一点可能会让人感到不舒服，因为八卦的名声确实不太好。

sentences.en: But it's actually really normal.
sentences.zh: 但它其实非常正常。

sentences.en: It's something that is really built into our society, into our human nature.
sentences.zh: 这是深深融入我们社会、融入我们人性之中的东西。

sentences.en: And I just think that it goes to show how much of our lives is really built around how we think about other people and built around the relationships that we share with others
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这恰恰说明了我们的生活中有多少内容，其实都是围绕着我们如何看待他人、围绕着我们与他人分享的关系构建的，

sentences.en: and our opinions on what they're doing and their opinions on us.
sentences.zh: 也是围绕着我们对他们行为的看法以及他们对我们的看法构建的。

sentences.en: I will say some of the takes, some of the things we'll discuss in this episode, you might not agree with.
sentences.zh: 我得说，本期节目中的某些观点和讨论内容，你可能并不认同。

sentences.en: And that's totally fine.
sentences.zh: 这完全没问题。

sentences.en: But I want to really bring a different perspective to this concept and discuss some of the science.
sentences.zh: 但我真的很想为这个概念带来不同的视角，并探讨一些科学依据。

sentences.en: Add a bit of colour into the conversation.
sentences.zh: 给对话增添一点趣味。

sentences.en: And hopefully, like we always aim to do, get you thinking about the role gossip may play in your own life.
sentences.zh: 希望就像我们一直以来所追求的那样，能引发你对八卦可能在你的生活中扮演的角色的思考。

sentences.en: So my lovely listeners, wherever you are, whatever time it may be, strap in, get ready, because today we're going to talk about the psychology behind gossip
sentences.zh: 所以，我可爱的听众们，无论你们身在何处，无论现在是什么时间，系好安全带，准备好吧，因为今天我们要聊聊八卦背后的心理，

sentences.en: and the hidden role it has to play in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 以及它在我们二十岁时所扮演的隐藏角色。

sentences.en: So gossip actually plays a really important role in our society.
sentences.zh: 所以八卦在我们的社会中其实扮演着非常重要的角色。

sentences.en: And in fairly unexpected ways as well.
sentences.zh: 而且是以相当出乎意料的方式。

sentences.en: Now I want to make a quick distinction here, or maybe a quick disclaimer.
sentences.zh: 现在我想在这里做一个快速的区分，或者说是一个简短的声明。

sentences.en: Gossip definitely gets a bad rap.
sentences.zh: 八卦的名声确实很糟糕。

sentences.en: And I think for some really, really good reasons.
sentences.zh: 我想这确实有一些非常非常充分的理由。

sentences.en: But also because of some of that confusion of what we are really talking about when we refer to gossip.
sentences.zh: 但也是因为我们在提到“八卦”这个词时，对它真正所指的内容产生了一些混淆。

sentences.en: I think when we typically think about the meaning of this word, we often get it confused with slander or lying, malicious rumours, tearing others down.
sentences.zh: 我想当我们通常想到这个词的含义时，经常会把它与诽谤、说谎、恶毒的谣言以及贬低他人混为一谈。

sentences.en: And there's certainly a dangerous element of gossip that gets mixed up in those things, especially when we use our words to hurt others
sentences.zh: 八卦中确实包含一些危险的成分，这些成分与上述种种混杂在一起，特别是当我们用言语去伤害他人，

sentences.en: or to look better in front of people we want to impress, which is honestly never a good idea.
sentences.zh: 或者为了在想要留下好印象的人面前显得更好时——说实话，这绝对不是什么好主意。

sentences.en: Or when we only ever have bad things to say about other people.
sentences.zh: 或者当我们对别人只有坏话可说的时候。

sentences.en: And I'm sure we've all met those people.
sentences.zh: 我相信大家都遇到过这样的人。

sentences.en: Maybe you've been that person at some stage in your life who finds themselves constantly saying negative things about other people, things you know aren't true.
sentences.zh: 也许你在人生的某个阶段也曾扮演过这样的人，发现自己 constamment（不断地）在说别人的坏话，说那些你明知不真实的事情。

sentences.en: And often it is to make yourself feel better.
sentences.zh: 通常这只是为了让自己感觉更好一点。

sentences.en: But I want to rewrite that conception.
sentences.zh: 但我想重塑这种观念。

sentences.en: I want to rewrite that definition for what we're talking about today.
sentences.zh: 我想重新定义我们今天所讨论的内容。

sentences.en: And what I mean when I refer to gossip throughout this episode is a way of sharing information by speaking in terms of others or speaking of others in a way
sentences.zh: 我在整期节目中提及八卦时所指的是一种分享信息的方式，即通过谈论他人或以某种方式谈论他人，

sentences.en: which is intended to convey a message, a story, a lesson, or an observation in the absence of that other person.
sentences.zh: 其目的是在当事人不在场的情况下，传达一个信息、一个故事、一个教训或一个观察结果。

sentences.en: You know, it most likely involves details about another person.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，它很可能包含关于另一个人的细节。

sentences.en: They don't always have to be negative details or private details, but details nonetheless.
sentences.zh: 这些细节不一定非要是负面的或是隐私的，但它们终究是细节。

sentences.en: And I guess you can make a personal judgment about whether that is in itself wrong.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以对这本身是否错误做出个人的判断。

sentences.en: Regardless of your opinion or how you define gossiping, we know that it exists.
sentences.zh: 无论你的观点如何，或者你如何定义八卦，我们都知道它的确存在。

sentences.en: In a 2019 study on the prevalence of gossip, these researchers, they found that on average
sentences.zh: 在2019年一项关于八卦普及率的研究中，这些研究人员发现，平均而言，

sentences.en: 52 minutes of our day is spent gossiping.
sentences.zh: 我们每天有52分钟花在八卦上。

sentences.en: But only about a quarter of that is actually negative.
sentences.zh: 但其中只有大约四分之一实际上是负面的。

sentences.en: And in another study, I think it was in the late 90s,
sentences.zh: 在另一项研究中，我想那是在90年代末，

sentences.en: 98, 97, this researcher,
sentences.zh: 98年、97年左右，这位研究人员，

sentences.en: Robin Dunbar, who's going to come up quite a bit in this episode, he suggested that gossip actually accounted for up to 65% of what we talk about with other people.
sentences.zh: 罗宾·邓巴（Robin Dunbar）——他在本期节目中会经常被提到——他指出，八卦实际上占了我们与他人交谈内容的65%。

sentences.en: So we obviously know that it is a part of the fabric of every society, even those that no longer exiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我们显然知道，它是每个社会结构的一部分，甚至是那些已经不复存在的社会。

sentences.en: You know, I'm sure there was heaps of gossip going around about
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我确信当年关于

sentences.en: Julius Caesar and Cleopatra back in the day.
sentences.zh: 尤利乌斯·凯撒和克莉奥帕特拉一定流传着大量的八卦。

sentences.en: So what I want to talk about is why it occurs.
sentences.zh: 所以我想谈谈它为什么会发生。

sentences.en: What are some of the evolutionary reasons, the psychological explanations behind why we gossip?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么会八卦，这背后有哪些进化论的原因和心理学解释？

sentences.en: Anthropologists and psychologists alike, they've been asking this question for some time and they have a few suggestions or opinions as to why gossip
sentences.zh: 人类学家和心理学家都在探讨这个问题有一段时间了，他们对于为什么八卦

sentences.en: might actually be a good thing.
sentences.zh: 其实可能是一件好事，提出了一些建议或观点。

sentences.en: And it's emerged to serve a social and evolutionary purpose.
sentences.zh: 它的出现是为了服务于社会和进化的目的。

sentences.en: The book Sapiens by Yuval Noah Harari.
sentences.zh: 尤瓦尔·赫拉利（Yuval Noah Harari）的书《人类简史》（Sapiens）。

sentences.en: It's a really good read if you're interested in this topic.
sentences.zh: 如果你对这个话题感兴趣，这是一本非常值得一读的好书。

sentences.en: And it explains how gossiping began to take place as humans began to construct bigger societies and develop broader social networks.
sentences.zh: 它解释了随着人类开始构建更大的社会并发展更广泛的社交网络，八卦是如何产生的。

sentences.en: As we moved away from small tribes, often in a hunter and gathering or agricultural environment and into larger villages and then cities, gossiping was a way to create in groups
sentences.zh: 当我们从狩猎采集或农业环境中的小型部落走向更大的村庄进而发展为城市时，八卦成为了一种在内部群体中建立信任的方式，

sentences.en: with those that we trusted and to inform those people who could be trusted and who could not.
sentences.zh: 并以此告知人们谁是值得信赖的，谁又是不可信的。

sentences.en: Gossiping is essentially a way of conveying what we see as important social information.
sentences.zh: 八卦本质上是一种传达我们认为重要的社会信息的方式。

sentences.en: And another perspective from the same evolutionary psychologist,
sentences.zh: 同一位进化心理学家提出了另一个观点，

sentences.en: Robin Dunbar, he suggests that gossip is actually a means of survival because it allows individuals to share valuable information about those in our social networks
sentences.zh: 罗宾·邓巴（Robin Dunbar）认为，八卦实际上是一种生存手段，因为它允许个人与一个大群体

sentences.en: with a large group.
sentences.zh: 分享关于我们社交网络中成员的宝贵信息。

sentences.en: You know, this could include warnings about dangerous or treacherous behavior that may jeopardize the group.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这可能包括对危险或可能危及群体的背叛行为的警告。

sentences.en: And as societies become larger, we couldn't observe every individual member's behavior like we were able to do in those intimate, smaller families and tribal groups.
sentences.zh: 随着社会变得越来越大，我们无法像在那些亲密的、较小的家庭和部落群体中那样观察到每个成员的行为。

sentences.en: So gossip became a way to monitor others' behavior and therefore maintain social cohesion.
sentences.zh: 因此，八卦成为监控他人行为并从而维持社会凝聚力的一种方式。

sentences.en: I think this sounds very detached from what we perceive as gossip-like these days.
sentences.zh: 我认为这听起来与我们如今所理解的八卦相去甚远——

sentences.en: You know, the very mean girl-esque picture of people sharing malicious rumors around the cafeteria table.
sentences.zh: 那种极其类似“塑料姐妹花”的画面，人们在自助餐厅的桌子旁分享恶毒的谣言。

sentences.en: But even in this scenario, the underlying evolutionary principle remains.
sentences.zh: 但即使在这种情况下，潜在的进化原则依然存在。

sentences.en: Gossip is nothing more than an advanced warning system for antisocial behavior.
sentences.zh: 八卦不过是针对反社会行为的一种预警系统。

sentences.en: You know, or freeloaders who may be taking advantage of the group or causing it harm.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，或者是针对那些可能在占群体便宜或给群体造成危害的“白嫖客”。
